decks.domain: Graduated licensing, tests, records and litter responsibility

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The secondary educational-document list includes a yearbook photograph, school records, or at least _____ report cards from different years.
cards.back: The secondary educational-document list includes a yearbook photograph, school records, or at least two report cards from different years.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: An original or certified professional degree or license, or a driver-education certificate, may serve as _____ documentation in the guide.
cards.back: An original or certified professional degree or license, or a driver-education certificate, may serve as secondary documentation in the guide.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The guide lists a Medicare or Medicaid card and a medical-eligibility card among _____ documents.
cards.back: The guide lists a Medicare or Medicaid card and a medical-eligibility card among secondary documents.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: _____ -document examples include original adoption papers, a baptismal certificate, and a Louisiana property deed or title, including a burial plot.
cards.back: Secondary-document examples include original adoption papers, a baptismal certificate, and a Louisiana property deed or title, including a burial plot.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A vehicle registration, a vehicle title in the applicant’s name, or a motor-vehicle lien document appears in the _____ -document list.
cards.back: A vehicle registration, a vehicle title in the applicant’s name, or a motor-vehicle lien document appears in the secondary-document list.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A utility statement showing the applicant’s name and address, or a receipt showing that utilities were activated, may be _____ documentation.
cards.back: A utility statement showing the applicant’s name and address, or a receipt showing that utilities were activated, may be secondary documentation.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The guide’s _____ -document list includes health, home, life or automobile insurance policies.
cards.back: The guide’s secondary-document list includes health, home, life or automobile insurance policies.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A printed payroll stub or wage-and-tax forms covering _____ years are listed as secondary documents.
cards.back: A printed payroll stub or wage-and-tax forms covering two years are listed as secondary documents.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The secondary-document list includes prison-release papers, a probation-officer letter, or _____ from a state agency responsible for placing a deprived or impaired person.
cards.back: The secondary-document list includes prison-release papers, a probation-officer letter, or verification from a state agency responsible for placing a deprived or impaired person.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Initial REAL ID issuance requires evidence of identity, lawful United States status, birth date and Social Security number, plus at least _____ documents showing the principal home address.
cards.back: Initial REAL ID issuance requires evidence of identity, lawful United States status, birth date and Social Security number, plus at least two documents showing the principal home address.

decks.domain: Graduated licensing, tests, records and litter responsibility

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A graduated learner permit limits driving to supervision by a fully licensed _____ .
cards.back: A graduated learner permit limits driving to supervision by a fully licensed driver.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The guide connects the higher crash risk of teenage drivers with _____ and immaturity.
cards.back: The guide connects the higher crash risk of teenage drivers with limited driving experience and immaturity.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Louisiana graduated licensing proceeds from a supervised learner permit to a restricted intermediate _____ and then a full license.
cards.back: Louisiana graduated licensing proceeds from a supervised learner permit to a restricted intermediate license and then a full license.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The first graduated-licensing stage requires an applicant to be at least _____ .
cards.back: The first graduated-licensing stage requires an applicant to be at least fifteen.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The learner stage requires _____ classroom hours and eight hours of behind-the-wheel instruction.
cards.back: The learner stage requires thirty classroom hours and eight hours of behind-the-wheel instruction.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The learner-stage applicant _____ pass the vision and knowledge examinations.
cards.back: The learner-stage applicant must pass the vision and knowledge examinations.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A learner-stage driver must be accompanied by a licensed adult aged at least _____ or a sibling aged at least eighteen.
cards.back: A learner-stage driver must be accompanied by a licensed adult aged at least twenty-one or a sibling aged at least eighteen.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Advancement from learner to intermediate requires holding the learner license at least _____ days and reaching the sixteenth birthday.
cards.back: Advancement from learner to intermediate requires holding the learner license at least one hundred eighty days and reaching the sixteenth birthday.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: For a _____ -year-old’s intermediate upgrade, a parent or legal guardian must attest to at least fifty driving-practice hours with a licensed parent, guardian or adult aged at least twenty-one, including fifteen hours at night.
cards.back: For a sixteen-year-old’s intermediate upgrade, a parent or legal guardian must attest to at least fifty driving-practice hours with a licensed parent, guardian or adult aged at least twenty-one, including fifteen hours at night.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The intermediate stage requires completing the learner stage and being at least _____ .
cards.back: The intermediate stage requires completing the learner stage and being at least sixteen.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The guide requires a road-skills score of at least _____ percent for intermediate licensing.
cards.back: The guide requires a road-skills score of at least eighty percent for intermediate licensing.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: An intermediate driver may not drive from _____ p.m. to five a.m. without a licensed adult aged at least twenty-one or a sibling aged at least eighteen.
cards.back: An intermediate driver may not drive from eleven p.m. to five a.m. without a licensed adult aged at least twenty-one or a sibling aged at least eighteen.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: From _____ p.m. to five a.m., an intermediate driver may carry no more than one passenger younger than twenty-one who is outside the immediate family.
cards.back: From six p.m. to five a.m., an intermediate driver may carry no more than one passenger younger than twenty-one who is outside the immediate family.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The intermediate license must be maintained until the driver turns _____ .
cards.back: The intermediate license must be maintained until the driver turns seventeen.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A full license follows successful completion of the learner and intermediate stages, or a first application made at age _____ or older.
cards.back: A full license follows successful completion of the learner and intermediate stages, or a first application made at age seventeen or older.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: An applicant aged _____ or older who has not entered graduated licensing may apply for a full Class E license or learner permit after a thirty-eight-hour driver-education course, or a six-hour pre-licensing course plus eight driving-instruction hours.
cards.back: An applicant aged eighteen or older who has not entered graduated licensing may apply for a full Class E license or learner permit after a thirty-eight-hour driver-education course, or a six-hour pre-licensing course plus eight driving-instruction hours.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A vehicle used on Louisiana highways _____ have liability insurance or another legally allowable substitute.
cards.back: A vehicle used on Louisiana highways must have liability insurance or another legally allowable substitute.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: At license issuance, an applicant _____ provide insurance evidence for vehicles the applicant owns.
cards.back: At license issuance, an applicant must provide insurance evidence for vehicles the applicant owns.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Acceptable insurance proof identifies the _____ , policy number, coverage dates, vehicle, insured person and insurer’s NAIC number.
cards.back: Acceptable insurance proof identifies the insurer, policy number, coverage dates, vehicle, insured person and insurer’s NAIC number.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The insurance card _____ remain in the vehicle as evidence of coverage.
cards.back: The insurance card must remain in the vehicle as evidence of coverage.

decks.domain: Graduated licensing, tests, records and litter responsibility

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A driver-license application may involve _____ screening, a traffic-law knowledge test and an on-road skills test.
cards.back: A driver-license application may involve vision screening, a traffic-law knowledge test and an on-road skills test.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: _____ is screened when a person applies for or renews a driver license or learner permit.
cards.back: Vision is screened when a person applies for or renews a driver license or learner permit.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The licensing vision screening is _____ a medical examination.
cards.back: The licensing vision screening is not a medical examination.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The guide states a minimum vision standard of _____ over forty for safe driving.
cards.back: The guide states a minimum vision standard of twenty over forty for safe driving.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A person who fails the _____ screening receives a report for a vision specialist to complete.
cards.back: A person who fails the vision screening receives a report for a vision specialist to complete.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: When corrective lenses are needed to pass vision screening, the license _____ wearing them while driving.
cards.back: When corrective lenses are needed to pass vision screening, the license requires wearing them while driving.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The corrective-lens restriction is displayed as code _____ on the license.
cards.back: The corrective-lens restriction is displayed as code one on the license.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: _____ laser correction, removing the lens restriction requires visiting OMV and passing screening without glasses or contact lenses.
cards.back: After laser correction, removing the lens restriction requires visiting OMV and passing screening without glasses or contact lenses.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Every first-time applicant must pass a knowledge test covering signs, signals, _____ driving and Louisiana driving laws.
cards.back: Every first-time applicant must pass a knowledge test covering signs, signals, safe driving and Louisiana driving laws.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The knowledge examination uses _____ questions drawn from the guide’s information.
cards.back: The knowledge examination uses multiple-choice questions drawn from the guide’s information.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Most offices administer the knowledge examination on a _____ .
cards.back: Most offices administer the knowledge examination on a computer.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A correct-answer rate of _____ percent is required to pass the knowledge examination.
cards.back: A correct-answer rate of eighty percent is required to pass the knowledge examination.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Proper identification is _____ whenever the knowledge examination is taken.
cards.back: Proper identification is required whenever the knowledge examination is taken.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The guide advises reading the manual at least _____ times before the written examination.
cards.back: The guide advises reading the manual at least three times before the written examination.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The guide advises reading the whole question and all answer choices _____ selecting an answer.
cards.back: The guide advises reading the whole question and all answer choices before selecting an answer.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The guide recommends arriving at least _____ hour before the office’s final testing time.
cards.back: The guide recommends arriving at least one hour before the office’s final testing time.

decks.domain: Graduated licensing, tests, records and litter responsibility

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The guide states that a driver license expires _____ years from the nearest birthday.
cards.back: The guide states that a driver license expires six years from the nearest birthday.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Renewal may be requested during the _____ days before license expiration.
cards.back: Renewal may be requested during the one hundred eighty days before license expiration.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A vision examination is _____ before a driver license is renewed.
cards.back: A vision examination is required before a driver license is renewed.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A newly issued license should be checked for correct information _____ leaving the office.
cards.back: A newly issued license should be checked for correct information before leaving the office.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The guide says _____ may cause a different expiration date for an immigrant, nonimmigrant or refugee.
cards.back: The guide says immigration status may cause a different expiration date for an immigrant, nonimmigrant or refugee.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: For qualifying service outside Louisiana, an Armed Forces or Peace Corps member’s license and qualifying dependents’ licenses remain valid for _____ days after discharge if valid on entering service.
cards.back: For qualifying service outside Louisiana, an Armed Forces or Peace Corps member’s license and qualifying dependents’ licenses remain valid for sixty days after discharge if valid on entering service.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Under that service rule, the license becomes expired or delinquent on the _____ -first day after discharge.
cards.back: Under that service rule, the license becomes expired or delinquent on the sixty-first day after discharge.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The last _____ and proof of discharge are accepted for renewal under the service-extension rule.
cards.back: The last license and proof of discharge are accepted for renewal under the service-extension rule.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A Louisiana resident younger than _____ with a Class D or E license may be selected for mail or internet renewal.
cards.back: A Louisiana resident younger than seventy with a Class D or E license may be selected for mail or internet renewal.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Mail or internet renewal invitations are not issued for _____ consecutive renewal cycles.
cards.back: Mail or internet renewal invitations are not issued for two consecutive renewal cycles.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A _____ who is offered mail or internet renewal may instead renew in person.
cards.back: A driver who is offered mail or internet renewal may instead renew in person.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A driver must update the address on a Louisiana license within _____ days after moving.
cards.back: A driver must update the address on a Louisiana license within ten days after moving.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A license name change may be supported by a _____ marriage license, a certified birth certificate for return to the birth name, or a certified court order authorizing the change.
cards.back: A license name change may be supported by a certified marriage license, a certified birth certificate for return to the birth name, or a certified court order authorizing the change.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A name change between renewals incurs a duplicate-_____ fee.
cards.back: A name change between renewals incurs a duplicate-license fee.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A lost, stolen or destroyed _____ may be replaced by applying in person at a motor-vehicle office.
cards.back: A lost, stolen or destroyed license may be replaced by applying in person at a motor-vehicle office.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: For a minor’s duplicate license, a _____ or domiciliary parent, tutor or legal guardian must appear with identification and custody documents to sign; with joint custody, only the domiciliary parent may sign.
cards.back: For a minor’s duplicate license, a custodial or domiciliary parent, tutor or legal guardian must appear with identification and custody documents to sign; with joint custody, only the domiciliary parent may sign.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A duplicate-license applicant _____ provide current liability-insurance proof for any registered vehicle.
cards.back: A duplicate-license applicant must provide current liability-insurance proof for any registered vehicle.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: OMV or a court may impose driving restrictions that appear on the _____ .
cards.back: OMV or a court may impose driving restrictions that appear on the license.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Violating a license restriction breaks the law and can cause _____ of driving privileges.
cards.back: Violating a license restriction breaks the law and can cause suspension of driving privileges.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The guide requires a detailed physician or vision-specialist report for a physically impaired first-time applicant or a first-time applicant older than _____ .
cards.back: The guide requires a detailed physician or vision-specialist report for a physically impaired first-time applicant or a first-time applicant older than sixty.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The _____ medical-report form must be obtained from OMV and must describe conditions that could impair safe driving.
cards.back: The required medical-report form must be obtained from OMV and must describe conditions that could impair safe driving.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: OMV may _____ anyone to provide a medical or vision report and may also require written or road-skills testing.
cards.back: OMV may require anyone to provide a medical or vision report and may also require written or road-skills testing.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: OMV keeps public records of traffic convictions and collisions for _____ years, while DWI convictions remain for ten years, including convictions received in other states.
cards.back: OMV keeps public records of traffic convictions and collisions for five years, while DWI convictions remain for ten years, including convictions received in other states.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A Louisiana identification card proves identity but does _____ authorize driving.
cards.back: A Louisiana identification card proves identity but does not authorize driving.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: An identification-card applicant _____ meet the identification requirements and have a valid Louisiana residential address.
cards.back: An identification-card applicant must meet the identification requirements and have a valid Louisiana residential address.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The guide lists a revoked license, unfinished required driver training, unpassed required tests and age below _____ as reasons a person is ineligible for a driver license.
cards.back: The guide lists a revoked license, unfinished required driver training, unpassed required tests and age below fifteen as reasons a person is ineligible for a driver license.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Altering _____ information, using a license unlawfully, or falsifying or hiding a material application fact can result in losing driving privileges.
cards.back: Altering license information, using a license unlawfully, or falsifying or hiding a material application fact can result in losing driving privileges.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: _____ to stop and assist after a collision involving injury or death can result in loss of driving privileges.
cards.back: Failing to stop and assist after a collision involving injury or death can result in loss of driving privileges.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A DWI conviction or refusal of an alcohol-analysis test _____ a DWI arrest can result in losing driving privileges.
cards.back: A DWI conviction or refusal of an alcohol-analysis test after a DWI arrest can result in losing driving privileges.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The guide lists an alcohol-test result of at least _____ point zero eight percent for a driver twenty-one or older, or at least zero point zero two percent for a driver younger than twenty-one, as grounds for losing driving privileges.
cards.back: The guide lists an alcohol-test result of at least zero point zero eight percent for a driver twenty-one or older, or at least zero point zero two percent for a driver younger than twenty-one, as grounds for losing driving privileges.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Failing to stop for a school bus while _____ are loading or unloading can result in loss of driving privileges.
cards.back: Failing to stop for a school bus while children are loading or unloading can result in loss of driving privileges.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: _____ -related manslaughter, negligent homicide or another felony committed while operating a vehicle can result in loss of driving privileges.
cards.back: Vehicle-related manslaughter, negligent homicide or another felony committed while operating a vehicle can result in loss of driving privileges.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: _____ reckless-driving convictions within twelve months can result in losing driving privileges.
cards.back: Three reckless-driving convictions within twelve months can result in losing driving privileges.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Unanswered traffic charges, violation of a license restriction, failure to meet financial-_____ requirements or driving while suspended can result in loss of driving privileges.
cards.back: Unanswered traffic charges, violation of a license restriction, failure to meet financial-responsibility requirements or driving while suspended can result in loss of driving privileges.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: An out-of-state _____ can affect Louisiana driving privileges when the same offense would support suspension or revocation in Louisiana.
cards.back: An out-of-state offense can affect Louisiana driving privileges when the same offense would support suspension or revocation in Louisiana.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The guide lists unpaid _____ or state income taxes as possible grounds for losing driving privileges.
cards.back: The guide lists unpaid child support or state income taxes as possible grounds for losing driving privileges.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Leaving school before graduation while aged _____ through seventeen, or being found habitually absent or tardy, can affect driving privileges.
cards.back: Leaving school before graduation while aged fifteen through seventeen, or being found habitually absent or tardy, can affect driving privileges.

decks.domain: Graduated licensing, tests, records and litter responsibility

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: _____ includes improperly leaving or discarding waste whether intentionally or unintentionally.
cards.back: Littering includes improperly leaving or discarding waste whether intentionally or unintentionally.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The guide distinguishes accidental simple _____ , deliberate intentional littering and gross littering involving large amounts of waste or an illegal dump.
cards.back: The guide distinguishes accidental simple littering, deliberate intentional littering and gross littering involving large amounts of waste or an illegal dump.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: _____ loads can shed objects that cause collisions, delays, injuries or deaths.
cards.back: Unsecured loads can shed objects that cause collisions, delays, injuries or deaths.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The guide attributes more than _____ point eight million Louisiana roadside litter pieces to a two thousand twenty-three Keep Louisiana Beautiful study.
cards.back: The guide attributes more than one hundred forty-three point eight million Louisiana roadside litter pieces to a two thousand twenty-three Keep Louisiana Beautiful study.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The guide attributes more than _____ percent of Louisiana roadside litter to motorists, pickup trucks, garbage trucks and unsecured loads.
cards.back: The guide attributes more than seventy-nine percent of Louisiana roadside litter to motorists, pickup trucks, garbage trucks and unsecured loads.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Cigarette butts are identified as the most littered small item and plastic water bottles as the most _____ littered roadside item in the guide’s cited study.
cards.back: Cigarette butts are identified as the most littered small item and plastic water bottles as the most visible littered roadside item in the guide’s cited study.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The cited study found more than _____ point nine million roadside plastic items, with plastic water bottles present at eighty percent of surveyed sites.
cards.back: The cited study found more than sixty-one point nine million roadside plastic items, with plastic water bottles present at eighty percent of surveyed sites.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The guide states that wind and rain move light roadside waste into waterways and that _____ percent of land litter eventually reaches a waterway.
cards.back: The guide states that wind and rain move light roadside waste into waterways and that eighty percent of land litter eventually reaches a waterway.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The guide explains that cigarette litter releases pollutants in _____ , may be eaten by wildlife, and has caused wildfires on land.
cards.back: The guide explains that cigarette litter releases pollutants in water, may be eaten by wildlife, and has caused wildfires on land.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Accidental and deliberate _____ are both unlawful and can lead to civil or criminal proceedings.
cards.back: Accidental and deliberate littering are both unlawful and can lead to civil or criminal proceedings.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: For simple littering, the guide lists a first-offense penalty of a _____ -dollar fine or eight community-service hours, rising for a second offense to nine hundred dollars or twenty community-service hours.
cards.back: For simple littering, the guide lists a first-offense penalty of a one hundred fifty-dollar fine or eight community-service hours, rising for a second offense to nine hundred dollars or twenty community-service hours.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A driver is responsible for litter leaving the vehicle or truck bed, including litter discarded by _____ .
cards.back: A driver is responsible for litter leaving the vehicle or truck bed, including litter discarded by passengers.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A loaded truck bed must be covered or secured so _____ and debris do not fall out.
cards.back: A loaded truck bed must be covered or secured so cargo and debris do not fall out.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A litter report should record the vehicle description and plate, plus the incident’s date, _____ and location, and the call should be made while parked.
cards.back: A litter report should record the vehicle description and plate, plus the incident’s date, time and location, and the call should be made while parked.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The guide reports _____ point four million dollars in annual Louisiana litter cleanup and prevention spending.
cards.back: The guide reports ninety-one point four million dollars in annual Louisiana litter cleanup and prevention spending.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The guide links litter with reduced property values, weaker business and tourism activity, _____ , flooding risk, harm to wildlife and reduced quality of life.
cards.back: The guide links litter with reduced property values, weaker business and tourism activity, blocked drainage, flooding risk, harm to wildlife and reduced quality of life.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Prevent litter by containing vehicle trash until it can be placed in a receptacle, requiring passengers _____ to litter, and keeping loose items from escaping a truck bed.
cards.back: Prevent litter by containing vehicle trash until it can be placed in a receptacle, requiring passengers not to litter, and keeping loose items from escaping a truck bed.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A smoker can keep a portable ashtray in the _____ rather than discard cigarette butts through a window.
cards.back: A smoker can keep a portable ashtray in the vehicle rather than discard cigarette butts through a window.
